correctness.rationale: Circle integration selects equal index sums of ordered triples. Independent Haar phases make the signed multiplicity vectors an orthonormal character basis, so subtracting the constant term makes variance the sum of squared coefficients. The identical-multiset cases (three distinct, one repeated, all equal) give 36 binom(n,3)+9n(n−1)+n. Cancel the common multiset on either side of a nonzero character: residual mass one is impossible by the equal-sum constraint. At mass two, four distinct indices admit a freely chosen common third index; it contributes 36 off that support and 18 on it, hence 36(n−2). Distinct signed pair characters have count (2n³+n)/12+O(n²), since the triangular pair-count energy is (2n³+n)/3, one coincidence costs a degree of freedom, and each character has four orderings. At mass three, the residual triples specify the original multisets; six distinct indices give exactly 36 orderings and coefficient 36. Independently, the ordered equal-sum triple energy equals the coefficient of z^(3n−3) in (1+⋯+z^(n−1))⁶ by reflecting the second triple. Inclusion–exclusion gives binom(3n+2,5)−6 binom(2n+2,5)+15 binom(n+2,5), hence (11/20)n⁵+O(n⁴). Coincidences leave at most five variables subject to a nontrivial linear equation, costing O(n⁴), so the signed character count is (11/720)n⁵+O(n⁴). With repeated residual indices, mass-two support ≤3 gives O(n²) characters with coefficient O(n); mass-three support ≤5 gives O(n⁴) with coefficient ≤36. All bounds use finitely many index patterns, giving absolute constants. Squaring the generic coefficients and summing gives 216+99/5=1179/5. Dividing by n⁶ and adding the O(n⁻²) squared bias gives the stated mean-square relation.
residual_risks: The proof uses Haar phase orthogonality; real signs do not yield the same character classification. No fluctuation limit or full finite-n variance polynomial is certified.

evidence: The integrated L⁶ power equals the squared coefficient norm of P_n³; variance is the squared norm of its nonconstant Fourier coefficients on the phase torus.

Choi–Mossinghoff treat this same normalized Lᵖ-power on Haar-unimodular polynomials. Benatar–Nishry–Rodgers use a random multiplicative coefficient model and study empirical distributions in the circle variable.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Matching 'Steinhaus' or 'Gaussian limit' is insufficient: coefficient independence and variance over phases, rather than circle sampling, define the statistic. The same-statistic result is genuine concentration overlap, not the sharp variance.

value.rationale: This quantifies the fluctuation scale and exact mean-square error of the first integrated even power beyond the fourth for a natural iid unimodular ensemble. The separation between inherited pair collisions and genuinely new triple collisions explains why a fourth-moment formula alone cannot give the constant. The result is a useful benchmark for quantitative concentration or fluctuation theorems without asserting a CLT.
residual_risks: No universality across coefficient distributions or frequency sets is claimed.
